welcome_lead: Time to apply teachings to divorce, contraception, sexuality and gender — and compare Christian and Muslim views.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Relationships application — divorce, contraception, sexuality, gender, comparing Christian and Muslim views.
final_note: You can now compare specific Christian and Muslim teachings on contemporary issues.

concepts.def: Declaration that a marriage was never valid
Choosing not to marry or have sex
Equal rights and dignity for men and women

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Roman Catholic Church does not allow divorce — only annulment if the marriage was invalid.

The Church of England permits divorce and sometimes remarriage in church.

Islam permits divorce (talaq) but Muhammad ﷺ said it is 'the most hated of permitted things' (Hadith). A waiting period (iddah) allows reconciliation.

Roman Catholic teaching (Humanae Vitae, 1968) opposes artificial contraception — marriage must be open to life.

Most Protestant churches and most Muslims permit contraception within marriage for spacing or health reasons, provided it does not cause abortion.

Traditional Christian and Muslim teachings limit sex to heterosexual marriage. Some Christian denominations (e.g. liberal Anglicans, Quakers, URC) now bless same-sex unions; Catholic and most Muslim teaching does not.

Galatians 3:28 — 'neither male nor female ... all one in Christ Jesus' — is used for gender equality. Qur'an 4:1 teaches men and women come from one soul.
